acceptanceCriteria.text: When a plan directory holds at least one top-level step artifact and no `*.state.json` and no `*.state.md` file, the observer shall report that directory as a state-less run.
If a plan directory holds neither a state file nor a step artifact, then the observer shall not report that directory as a run.
The observer shall emit one `run-without-state` finding per state-less run, naming the newest step artifact in the finding evidence as a repo-relative path.
While the newest step artifact of a state-less run is at most one effective stall window old, the observer shall report the `run-without-state` finding at `warning` severity.
When the newest step artifact of a state-less run is older than the effective stall window, the observer shall report the `run-without-state` finding at `info` severity.
The observer shall resolve the state-less freshness window from the same effective stall window as the liveness stopwatch, defaulting to 600 seconds when `--stall-window` is not supplied.

The observer shall include every detected state-less run in `workflowCount` and shall suppress the line `No workflow state files found under the configured plans directory.` while at least one state-less run is reported.
The observer shall count a state-less run whose newest step artifact is inside the effective stall window toward `activeCount`, so `--watch --until-terminal` does not stop while that run is fresh.

While a state-less run is older than the effective stall window, the observer shall keep its finding visible and shall not count the run toward `activeCount`, so an unattended `--until-terminal` watch can still terminate.
When a plan directory holds a state file, the observer shall classify it through the existing state path and shall not emit a `run-without-state` finding for it.
When `--slug <slug>` scopes a snapshot and `{plansDir}/<slug>/` holds no state file, the observer shall resolve the state-less run by plan directory name and report it for that slug.
The observer shall expose a state-less run record with `statePath` null, unknown step and verification fields, and the newest step artifact as repo-relative evidence.

The observer shall derive state-less activity evidence from the canonical top-level `step-NN-{slug}.*` step-artifact naming already used by `expectedArtifacts()`, and shall treat no other file class as activity.
The observer shall bound the state-less scan to the top-level entries of each plan directory and shall not descend into nested directories such as plan worktrees.
If a plans-root entry is not a readable directory, then the observer shall skip it without failing the snapshot or suppressing findings for other runs.
The observer shall keep the multi-spec `missing-child-state` signal unchanged in trigger, severity, and evidence, and shall not replace it with `run-without-state`.

The observer shall add `run-without-state` to the `DEFECT_CONTRACTS` map so an `--open-issue` proposal names the discovery contract for that code, while dedupe and severity classification stay with the existing finding helper.
The observer shall leave the configured plans directory unchanged, creating, modifying, and deleting no file during state-less detection.
The ws-monitor skill documentation shall list `run-without-state` with its freshness-to-severity rule in the signal map and in the actionable-signals list.

negativeScenarios.text: Red test: a plan directory holding only a state file and no `step-NN-` artifact must produce no `run-without-state` finding and must keep `workflowCount` unchanged, pinning the precondition that protects the us-464 and us-395 zero-count assertions.
Red test: a directory holding neither a state file nor a step artifact (an empty scratch folder, or a folder holding only `worktrees/`) must not appear in `workflows` and must not raise the finding.

Red test: a directory whose state file is malformed or truncated must still go down the existing state path and must never raise `run-without-state` — state presence is the discriminator, not parse success.

Red test: a state-less run whose newest artifact is older than the effective stall window must report `info` and must not increment `activeCount`, so `--until-terminal` still terminates on an abandoned directory.
Red test: at the window boundary (artifact age equal to the window) severity must be `warning`, not `info`.
Red test: `--workflow-id <unknown-id>` must not match a state-less directory and must leave `workflowCount` at 0 for that selector.
Red test: nested artifacts such as `demo/worktrees/<slug>/step-00-x.spec.md` or a `.runtime/` marker must not count as activity for the top-level run.

Red test: a plans-root entry that is not a readable directory — including the `{plansDir}/index.json` file and a permission-denied directory — must be skipped without failing the snapshot, while a sibling state-less run in the same root is still reported.

Regression assertion: run the monitor suites and assert `missing-child-state`, the us-464 slug-scoping counts, the us-395 `activeCount === 0` check, and the watch-profile expectations still pass unchanged.
Contract assertion: assert `ws-monitor/SKILL.md` names `run-without-state` together with the fresh-`warning` / stale-`info` rule, so documentation cannot drift from the code.

Stack-safety assertion: assert no file is created under the fixture plans root during a snapshot and that the diff contains no Python file, no new runtime dependency, and no ESM/launcher change (node-skills-package invariant).
